script: NBA players who gave up MILLIONS of dollars and it actually PAID OFF! In 2004, Shaquille O'Neal demanded a trade from the Lakers after the front office refused to give him a max contract extension, and the tension between him and Kobe Bryant had gotten so bad that the two could barely coexist on the same team. So the Lakers traded Shaq to the Miami Heat, where he'd play alongside a young Dwyane Wade. But what Shaq did next completely contradicted everything that just happened in LA. After his first season in Miami, Pat Riley sat Shaq down and gave him two options. Option one was a $120 million extension, but the roster stays thin. Option two was $100 million, and Riley gets enough cap space to surround him and Wade with real players. Shaq looked at $20 million sitting on the table, walked away from it, and told Riley he needed to win. So Riley went to work, bringing in Gary Payton and Antoine Walker while keeping Udonis Haslem to build out a roster that actually had depth. But the part that makes this story hit different is what happened next. In the 2006 NBA Finals against Dallas, the Heat went down 0-2 before Wade took over and dropped forty-two points in Game three, and Miami rattled off four straight wins to take the championship. Shaq got his fourth ring, and the guy who left the Lakers partly because they wouldn't pay him enough became the guy who voluntarily gave up $20 million just to make sure he could win one more.
